docs.text: MangoPulse CMS Introduction MangoPulse content management system, often abbreviated as CMS, is a software that helps users create, manage, and modify content on a website without the need for specialized technical knowledge. It helps you build a website without needing to write all the code from scratch. Instead of building your own system for creating web pages, storing images, and other functions, MangoPulse CMS handles all that basic infrastructure stuff for you so that you can easily edit your website. The current documentation contains several functionalities and uses of ADMedia CMS. CMS Guide CMS guide contains different details related to website content management. It defines post types and how it could be created, edited and published. Setup of New Subscription To set up a new subscription, several steps must be followed to onboard a new website. System Architecture Describes the different system components and their corresponding Azure services. Modules Describes several important modules that add extra functionalities to the core system, e.g: Podcast, CMS API, Search, and Mobile API.

docs.text: Al Ittihad API Documentation Introduction All API calls are mentioned using API_BASE_URL to designate the main domain for the API, e.g. https://beta-api.alittihad.ae/ . Page Structure A page has some info, and an array of blocks (Sections/Widgets) which represent the data related to this page, where each block can contain a post (array consisting of single post) or array of posts. A Block is a collection of posts (articles, videos...). It knows what style to use in order to display those posts. A post can be an article, video… It has a title, media (which can be cover image, video, audio...), metas (author, location…) and Tag. Page/Article Details Definition Pages are the screens in the web app (TV, Home, Subscribe, podcasts…) and they can be reached when a menu item is clicked, or when articles are clicked. Article details page is the screen got when tapping an article. It contains the details of that article, including paragraphs, author, tags... It also contains additional recommended articles section. Structure Both pages and article details have the same data structure as shown in the code block below. They both have Blocks(Widgets) that are the actual sections and parts of this page. { "PageInfo": {...}, "JsonLD": {...}, "Blocks": [ {...}, {...}, {...}, ] } The only difference is that article details should contain a specific block: style=details (or details_ext ). In this case, the posts array should contain only one post, which has the needed info. That’s why it is recommended to build a centralized controller that handle an array of blocks. NOTE: The PageInfo contains: Page.PublicId : used for tracking page visits. Page.PageTitle : shown in the header. Page’s Anatomy Each Page is composed of an array of Blocks. Each Block has a title, style, and is composed of array of Posts (articles, videos...), where the title is a key to identify the block. { "PageInfo": {...}, "JsonLD": {...}, "Blocks": [ { "Id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000", "Title": "كاريكاتير", "Content": null, "MoreLink": "posts?type=caricature", "LoadMoreLink": "posts/loadmore/caricature?widget=caricature&type=caricature&page=2", "Order": 1, "Location": "Content", "Style": "List", "Type": "sync", "ViewOptions": {...}, "Posts": {...}, "Terms": null, "Ad": null, "SeoSettings": {...}, "Comments": null }, {...}, {...} ] } API Calls The following pages contain the needed API calls to common page's JSON structure. Home Page The home page contains a lot of widgets. https://beta-api.alittihad.ae/v3/posts/4144671?platform=mobile&target=ios Widgets Definition Widgets are the building Blocks that form the web page. Below is the structure of a widget: { "Id": "9366e152-8609-11e9-80bf-0cc47a86a49", "Title": null, "Content": null, "MoreLink": "null", "Order": 1, "Location": "Content", "Style": "Slider_Big", "ViewOptions": {...}, "Posts": [...], "Terms": null, "Ad": null, "SeoSettings": null, "Comments": null } Structure The widget has the following fields: - Title - LoadMoreLink The LoadMoreLink is called as follows, where posts are taken from the first widget and current posts are appended to the returned posts. {API_BASE_URL}/v3/{LoadMoreLink}&platform=mobile&target=ios Style The Style dictates how posts are displayed. - Posts It is a collection of articles/videos. Post A Post have a lot of attributes, but we show only few of them in the widget (Unless it’s a details widget). The post attributes are as follows: { "Guid": "2175baa4-206f-11ec-b76a-501ac508383f", "Views": 35, "PublicId": 4224460, "Title": "كاريكاتير الاتحاد", "ShortTitle": null, "Summary": "", "PostDate": "2021-09-29T00:15:00", "DisplayDate": "28, سبتمبر", "PublicUrl": "https://beta.alittihad.ae/caricature/4224460/كاريكاتير-الاتحاد", "PostType": {...}, "Terms": [], "ShortLink": "https://beta.alittihad.ae/caricature/4224460/كاريكاتير-الاتحاد", "Order": 0, "Medias": {...}, "Metas": [], "Relatives": [], "Content": "", "Shares": 0, "SubPosts": [], "PostAds": null, "Label": null, "Tag": null, "Action": "image" } PublicId: The PublicId is used to generate the post details page, e.g: {api_url}/v3/posts/{post.publicId}?platform=mobile&target=ios Where the PublicId is reached from the posts of the related listing page. The full HTML text that represents the actual article (provided only for Details Pages) Metas: An array of meta data (author, director, location...) - ShortLink: The ShortLink is used to share a post. PostType: Video Episode Article These keywords can be used to query the API for more posts of a certain post-type. Post's Tags A Tag is a classifier that you can use in the API to get similar posts. If needed use Tag.Title to display this tag. When clicked, send an API request as follows: https://beta-api.alittihad.ae/v3/posts/{Tag.Url}?platform=mobile&target=ios A sample tag has the following attributes: "Tag": { "Title": "الإمارات", "Style": "#569fd7", "Url": "posts?taxonomy=category&term=الإمارات", "Label": "القسم" } Post's Images/Media Media All media related to a post are collected in this array. Media.Type Can be one of these values: video , image , or audio . Media.Placement Indicates how to use this media. It has the following values: Cover , Main , and Gallery . Cover : the media is an image that is used to represent this post in a widget. Main : the media is a playable media item. It might be a video (youtube, stream), audio file (mp3). It can be used to start the player when needed. Gallery : the media should be displayed in a carousel or grid when the post details is clicked. The image can be resized to best fit, and save bandwidth by appending to Media.Thumbnail as follows: Media.Thumbnail + "?width={w}&height={h}" where w & h are the desired width and height. docs.text: The authentication is implemented using JSON Web Tokens (JWT). At first, a user logs in via /login API, providing his username and password . The response is an access token and a refresh token . The access token is valid for 24 hours, while the refresh token is valid for 48 hours. The access token will be sent in the Authorization header in every subsequent authorized API request. Once the access token is expired, a client side logic should be implemented to get a new access token by providing the available refresh token . This is done using via /refreshtoken API. The response in this case is a new access token and a new refresh token . When the user logs out, a request will be sent to /logout API to invalidate the available refresh token . NOTE: The user should be created in the ADMedia Admin panel. Login POST /user/login Type Parameters Description Required Request body Username The user name true Password The user password true Response body accessToken JSON object with two fields: Token exprires refreshToken success The status of the request: true or false Success example: { "accessToken": { "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1bmlxdWVfbmFtZSI6InRlY2hzdXBwb3J0IiwiaWQiOiIwYjQyMjE3Yi1lNTc1LTQ5ZTMtODQ4Mi1hMzcxMDBjZDc2ZGYiLCJzdWIiOiJ0ZWNoc3VwcG9ydCIsIm5iZiI6MTYyODU4MjkwNSwiZXhwIjoxNjI4NjY5MzA1LCJpYXQiOjE2Mjg1ODI5MDV9.6vn4ktEiUm7DQUk4hokiJLNTAMUxowS6I-aYjFIJk6g", "expires": "2021-08-11T08:08:25.7901289Z" }, "refreshToken": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1bmlxdWVfbmFtZSI6InRlY2hzdXBwb3J0IiwiaWQiOiIwYjQyMjE3Yi1lNTc1LTQ5ZTMtODQ4Mi1hMzcxMDBjZDc2ZGYiLCJzdWIiOiJ0ZWNoc3VwcG9ydCIsIm5iZiI6MTYyODU4MjkwNSwiZXhwIjoxNjI4NzU1NzA1LCJpYXQiOjE2Mjg1ODI5MDV9.MS1lpnibMJLboBO90vjYTi4EgWZga9wEe5TIDvnI5Ww", "success": true } Failure example: { "errors": [ { "code": "login_failure", "description": "Invalid username or password." } ], "success": false } Logout Make sure to delete the access token and refresh token from client side storage (cookies, ...). docs.text: The CMS API is a module that enable third parties to create and publish posts without using the default CMS. To use the CMS API it is required to have the subscriptionCode and the postTypeCode . Examples of subscriptionCode : alitihad for alittihad.ae . zak for zahratalkhaleej.ae . Examples of postTypeCode : news for alittihad.ae . article for zahratalkhaleej.ae . NOTE: The postTypeCode should be requested from the Admin administrators.

docs.text: The following are the steps to create an index and index the existing data. Before index creation, it’s advised to save words that don’t need stemming. For that matter, I attached a text file ( keywords.txt) including the list of countries in Arabic. We may add other words to this file using the two APIs below (for better search results): Update Meta API POST /keywords/update_meta Type Parameters Description Required Request body file Keywords file name true This API saves the list of meta specified in specific post types (specifying meta and post types are configured from our side). For example, an author is a meta of news. The keywords file name is the full path of the keywords file. For example: D:/elasticsearch-6.5.1/elasticsearch-6.5.1/config/keywords.txt Update Titles API POST /keywords/update_titles Type Parameters Description Required Request body file Keywords file name true This API is used to save titles of posts with certain post types (configured from our side as well) in case they are considered as keywords. The author post type is an example. Index Creation API To create an index with Arabic language. POST /indices Type Parameters Description Required Request body index index name true keywords keywords file name language 10: arabic 30: english true NOTE: The keywords file is the text file located in the config folder inside the ElasticSearch folder containing words that shouldn’t be stemmed. Example: json { "index": "ar", "keywords": "keywords.txt", "language": 10 } Index Existing Data API POST /documents/add_saved Type Parameters Description Required Request body index index name true from The page number from which we start saving data, 1 by default to The last page number from which we save data fromdate The date from which we start saving data. (YYYY/MM/dd) todate The date which won’t be exceeded. (YYYY/MM/dd) body List of excluded post type codes Make sure you send the following body parameter: (in addition to all types that shouldn’t be indexed): ["templates"] Index Generated Data API POST /documents/add_generated Type Parameters Description Required Request url index index name true That’s how you save existing data in your index. Newly created posts will be automatically indexed once published, and will no longer be indexed when withdrawn. Docs Count API GET /indices/{name}/get_docs_count Type Parameters Description Required Request url name index name true Response count Number of documents Docs Count API GET /indices/{name}/get_client_docs_count Type Parameters Description Required Request url name index name true Response count Number of documents Delete Index API POST /indices/{name}/delete Type Parameters Description Required Request url name index name true Delete Subscription' Documents API POST /documents/delete_client_docs Type Parameters Description Required Request url name index name true Re-index Documents API In case, the keywords file has changed, and you want to consider the newly added keywords, make sure you re-index the existing data with this API. POST /indices/{name}/reindex Type Parameters Description Required Request url name index name true body keywords keywords file name true language 10: arabic 30: english true Re-index Documents API (Internal) Another API is called on daily basis to re-index failed documents. POST /documents/reindex Type Parameters Description Required Request url index index name true size The count of las posts published to be re-indexed true overwrite Overwrite already indexed posts or not

docs.text: Definition Pages are the screens in the mobile app (TV, Home, Subscribe, podcasts…) and they can be reached when a menu item is clicked, or when articles are clicked. NOTE: You will have to manually create static pages, such as: subscription, registration, ... Article details page is the screen got when tapping an article. Structure Both pages and article details have the same data structure as shown in the code block below. They both have Blocks(Widgets) that are the actual sections and parts of this page. { "PageInfo": {...}, "JsonLD": {...}, "Blocks": [ {...}, {...}, {...}, ] } The only difference is that article details should contain a specific block: style=details (or details_ext ). In this case, the posts array should contain only one post, which has the needed info. That’s why it is recommended to build a centralized controller that handle an array of blocks. NOTE: The PageInfo contains: Page.PublicId : used for tracking page visits. Page.PageTitle : shown in the header. Page’s Anatomy Each Page is composed of an array of Blocks. Each Block has a title, style, and is composed of array of Posts (articles, videos...).

docs.text: This documentation is tailored to help mobile developers to build the mobile apps on both platforms: android and iOS. All API calls are mentioned using API_BASE_URL to designate the main domain for the API, e.g. api.zahratalkhaleej.ae . Both Android and iOS developers can use this API, but the used platform should be mentioned in the URL, as query string parameters, for analytics purposes: Examples: - https://API_BASE_URL/v3/posts/123?platform=mobile&target=ios - https://API_BASE_URL/v3/posts/123?platform=mobile&target=android Page Structure A page has some info, and an array of blocks (Sections/Widgets) which represent the data related to this page, where each block can contain a post or array of posts. A Block is a collection of posts (articles, videos...). It knows what style to use in order to display those posts. A post can be an article, video… It has a title, media (which can be cover image, video, audio...), metas (author, location…) and Tag.

docs.text: Configuration To load the configuration of your app, which contains a Menus section, an API call should be made to the following link, which contains a Menus section: https://API_BASE_URL/v3/configs Each menu type is an array of menu items and each might have sub-menus . OnClick event for all menu items should have the same behavior. { "OrganizationInfo": {...}, "Styling": {...}, "Menus": { "m-main2": [...], "m-main3": [...], "m-main": [...], "m-full": [...] }, "Topics": [], "SearchCategories": [...], "InterstitialFrequency": 2, "AdvancedTracking": true } Menu Types There is two types of menus: 1- Main Contains the main prominent pages, and access to the full menu. The menu will be dynamically loaded from API's response. It provides dynamic pages only. Any other menu items (full menu icon, settings, profile...) should be added manually. NOTE: The menu items should be matched with their suitable icons. 2- Full A big menu with lots of links and social media presence. The menu will be dynamically loaded from API's response. NOTE: The social media icons should be loaded manually. Menu Item The main elements in a menu item are: Title Url: Destination page. This should be concatenated with {API_BASE_URL}/v3/{MenuItem.Url}, e.g: https://api.zahratalkhaleej.ae/v3/MenuItem.Url?platform=mobile&target={android/ios} Examples https://api.zahratalkhaleej.ae/v3/posts/942476?platform=mobile&target=ios https://api.zahratalkhaleej.ae/v3/posts?type=article&category=celebrities&platform=mobile&target=ios Submenus: if available, they behave the same way as a regular menu item. Others elements: optional.

docs.text: Definition Widgets are the building Blocks that form the mobile page. Below is the structure of a widget: { "Id": "9366e152-8609-11e9-80bf-0cc47a86a49", "Title": null, "Content": null, "MoreLink": "null", "Order": 1, "Location": "Content", "Style": "Slider_Big", "ViewOptions": {...}, "Posts": [...], "Terms": null, "Ad": null, "SeoSettings": null, "Comments": null } Structure The widget has the following fields: - Title - LoadMoreLink The LoadMoreLink is called as follows, where posts are taken from the first widget and current posts are appended to the returned posts. {API_BASE_URL}/v3/{LoadMoreLink}&platform=mobile&target=ios Style The Style dictates how posts are displayed. - Posts It is a collection of articles/videos. Post A Post have a lot of attributes, but we show only few of them in the widget (Unless it’s a details widget). The post attributes are as follows: - PublicId: The PublicId is used to generate the post details page, e.g: {api_url}/v3/posts/post.publicId?platform=mobile&target=ios Title PostDate Summary Content The full HTML text that represents the actual article (provided only for Details Pages, put it in a webview) Metas: An array of meta data (author, director, location...) - ShortLink: The ShortLink is used to share a post. PostType: Video Episode Article These keywords can be used to query the API for more posts of a certain post-type. Post's Tags A Tag is a classifier that you can use in the API to get similar posts. If needed use Tag.Title to display this tag. When clicked, send an API request as follows: https://api.zahratalkhaleej.ae/v3/posts/{Tag.Url}?platform=mobile&target=ios A sample tag has the following attributes: "Tag": { "Title": "الإمارات", "Style": "#569fd7", "Url": "posts?taxonomy=category&term=الإمارات", "Label": "القسم" } Post's Images/Media Media All media related to a post are collected in this array. Media.Type Can be one of these values: video , image , or audio . Media.Placement Indicates how to use this media. It has the following values: Cover , Main , and Gallery . Cover : the media is an image that is used to represent this post in a widget. Main : the media is a playable media item. It might be a video (youtube, stream), audio file (mp3). It can be used to start the player when needed. Gallery : the media should be displayed in a carousel or grid when the post details is clicked. The image can be resized to best fit, and save bandwidth by appending to Media.Thumbnail as follows: Media.Thumbnail + "?width={w}&height={h}" where w & h are the desired width and height.

docs.text: Admin Audit You can reach Audit from admin panel Logs ar actions which happened in the system. You can search and filter these logs using the filter bar on top of the audit table including: Date: date range filtering actions by the date they happened User: the user causing the action Title: title of the action; e.g. post title Type: post type Operation: the action done Browser: the browser the action happened from. Users You can reach users from the admin panel under "User Management" User have status with 2 options: Active, Inactive. You can activate/deactivate a user from the list of users or from the preview page. The preview page also includes a button to check the audit of this user. From the listing page, click the plus icon to add a new user A user should have a unique name Password should match the validation policy. The role of the user defines the set of permissions of this user Language is the default language for this user Roles You can reach roles from the "Admin Panel" under "User Management". The role defines an access level. It can be assigned to multiple users. It has status options: Active, Inactive. You can toggle between options from the roles listing page or the edit page. To create a role enter name, description and tick the allowed permissions. To disable a permission click it again.

docs.text: Widgets can easily be configured and arranged and give users more control over the look and functionality over the website. Each widget contain several settings Widget Properties Contains the main properties of the widget Description: A brief explanation about the widget, e.g. Latest news Latest news 1 Code: The unique code for every widget in a page or template Main Content: If enabled, it displays the current content in the main. Order: The order of the widget, e.g. if there are multiple ads widgets in a single page, it changes their orders Platforms: The platforms where this widget is used, e.g. mobile, website or TV. More than one platform can be selected from the displayed list. Widget Display Contains the display options of the widget Title: The title that is displayed in Arabic language, e.g. أهم الأخبار Title En: The title that is displayed in English language, e.g. Top News More Links: Desired URL in case of a button "اقرأ المزيد", e.g. الأخبار/ Group Of Widgets: If enabled, they are used in the website if the Html contain tabs or menu and we need multiple widgets to be used in the same Razor View Cashe Duration: To specify the time needed for the cache Load Type: One loading method is selected from a dropdown list, e.g. sync, async or both Refresh Interval: The duration between two refresh Delay: The delay in seconds which is used for the async. Show on PC: If enabled, the widget will be displayed when opened on a desktop Show on Mobile: If enabled, the widget will be displayed when opened on a mobile. Hide: If enabled, the widget won't be displayed View Title: Enable to display title (the displayed length can be specified), e.g. 15 View Summary: Enable to display summary (the displayed length can be specified) View Date: Enable to display the date (the date format used can be specified) Cover Display: Enable to display the cover photo (the source, ratio, and crop size can be specified) Infinite Scroll Index: Enable if infinite scroll is supported (the widget index among the scrolls is specified) Playable: Enable if the cover is playable Show Related Inside Article: Enable to display related posts inside the body of the current post Split Content: Enable to split the body of the post to insert other elements post Include Coverage: Enable if the the post has related coverage and it's desired to display it Show Tags: Enable to display included tags (specify the type of tags, e.g. category or classification). Show Author: Enable to display author's name Show More: Enable to provide load more option Load On Scroll: Enable to load more automatically when scrolling Metas Social Actions Custom Style: e.g. inch Groups Widget View Options Contains the view name that reflects this widget: Web, Mobile, TV, FacebookBot and AMP. Web Website Logo: logo image considered as a symbol of identification Web View: The targeted format for the view on the website (provide the path for the code used), e.g. Static/Logo Logo source: to locate the source of logo image. Mobile Mobile View: The targeted format for the view on the mobile (provide the path for the code used), e.g. list TV TV View: The targeted format for the view on the TV (provide the path for the code used) FaceBook Bot FaceBook Bot View: The targeted format for the view on the facebook(provide the path for the code used) AMP AMP View: The targeted format for the view on the Amp(provide the path for the code used) Widget Data Source Contains the source of data for the widget Data Source: Where does this widget get the data from, e.g. the current list or the terms. It is displayed as a dropdown list. Database View: It is a subset of database. Source Identification: specifies the primary source from where it comes from Post Types: The post types displayed in this widget, e.g. Author. More than one type can be selected. Status: To identify the status of the widget if published or not. Terms: To identify the terms of the widget Tags: To identify the tags of the widget Exclude Tags: Exclude the posts under the specified tags All Tags: If enabled, all tags are included Current Tags: Show posts under the current tags only (used for filtering the posts) Related To: e.g. current or front user. Subscriptions: The clients using this widget (Ex.: Alittihad, Mangopulse..) Order: The criteria to organize the posts, e.g. p.PostDate DESC to organized posts by date in descending order From the date of: The first date allowed for a displayed post To the date of: The latest date allowed for a displayed post Expiration time in minutes: Expiry date in minutes (Ex: used for urgent news..) Size: Total number of posts included in the widget Exclude Current Post: Enable to exclude the current post from the list Exclude Global Date Filter: Enable to exclude the global date from filtering Posts Per Type: Number of posts for each type (if multiple types included) Page: To return the specified page Skip: Number of posts to skip before the ones to be displayed Head Scripts: to specify the head scripts Scripts Widget Structure Contains the data related to the widget Get Media: If enabled, the widget will import the media of the post Get Terms: If enabled, the widget will import the terms of the post Get Metas: If enabled, the widget will import the meta data of the post Get Sub Posts: If enabled, the widget will import the sub posts Get Up Relatives: If enabled, the widget will import the up relatives of the post Get Down Relatives: If enabled, the widget will import the down relatives of the post Get Links: If enabled, the widget will import the links relative to each post Include Summary: If enabled, the summary of the post will be included Include Content: If enabled, the content will be displayed Include Content In Query: If enabled, the content will be displayed in the query Relate Terms To Post Types: If enabled, the term will be attached to the post type Included Media: A list of the media that should be included Included Meta: A list of the metadata that should be included Included Terms: A list of the terms that should be included Widget Advertisements Contains the advertisements related to the widget Web Desktop Advertisement: The type of ad to be displayed on the website when used on a desktop Web Mobile Advertisement: The type of ad to be displayed on the website when used on mobile Android Advertisement: The type of ad to be displayed on an android device IOS Advertisement: The type of ad to be displayed on an IOS device Tv Advertisement: The type of ad to be displayed on a TV Amp Advertisement: The type of ad to be displayed on AMP

docs.text:
Post Type You can reach "Post Types" page from "tools and setup" Configuring a post type indicates the template which will be used by posts of this type. The post type page consists of the following tabs: General Title: The title for the post type displayed on the Admin panel, e.g. مقالات Code: The unique code for the post type used in the URLs to identify the current post type. Child: Used to assign a child for the post type example (Article and Parts), [it's used also in Post Search (GetChildren: true) with a Role ‘child’ and filled in post SubPosts], e.g. the episode post type can be added as a child for the show post type. Custom Javascript: The script to be executed on the post form related events, e.g. to prevent saving an empty summary for a post write a script that fills it from content if empty. Image: The image of the post type used in the Admin panel. Meta Data Key: The key used for getting this metadata in the code., e.g. photographer. This is used to distinguish between meta when displaying them on the front. Display: The title that appears in the post form, e.g. المصور. FieldType: The type of the data (Ex: text, list, …). Text: It displays the input in the form of text. TextArea: It displayed a text area for multiline text. Editor: It displayed a tinymce HTML editor. CheckBox: It displayed a checkbox. Map: It displays a geographic map. Date: It displays a date picker. DateTime: It displays a datetime picker. TimeSpan: A timespan describes an interval within the item. qaaq YearPicker: It displays a year picker. DayPicker: It displays a day picker. DayName: It displays a day picker. MonthPicker: It displays a month picker. List: It will check the Data source prop if it contains “,” it will show the comma separated data (item1,item2,item3…) It is a “|” separated field like (source|Name) it will fetch the list of terms for a Taxonomy named “source” Enum: It displays Items from the enum defined in DataSource, Enum are hard coded Color: It displays a color picker. The displayed colors are implemented in the StyleConfig class. They are listed in the AvailableColorsinput field. Hidden: not accessible to view. MangomoloAudioCategory: It fetches categories from Mangomolo audio categories API MangomoloVideoCategory: It fetches categories from Mangomolo video categories API Required: If enabled, it's mandatory in the post form (true/false). Icon: meta icon Order: Data order appearance in the post form. DataSource: If it contains “,” It is a “|” separated field like (source|Name) it will fetch the list of terms for a Taxonomy named “source”. Only used when type is list (comma separated). Default: Used if FieldType is "date" or FieldType is "datetime”, if it is "[NOW]” it will be calculated and filled in code. If this meta is not filled, this value will be saved upon saving a post. Role: The data role (e.g. display: in case we need to display this meta on the website, link, icon, Youtube, Map). Public: if true, this can be shown on the website. ShowInList: if enabled,the meta is displayed as a column in the posts table in the admin panel. HiddenInitially: If enabled, the field will be hidden in the form until added. Media Compress: If enabled, media will be compressed. Count: Number of media allowed 0,1,2....n or * 1 if infinity, e.g. if the count for المحتوى is 3, it allows the user to add only three items for the selected type "Video". After adding two videos, UploadVideo option is still available because count is set to 3 so one more video can be added. After adding the third video, UploadVideo option is no longer available. Placement: The term used for handling media items in the code, e.g. cover, main, editor or gallery. It’s possible to create any new placement, that way you need to handle it in the code. cover: Once added, can be found under the details tab in post creation form. It’s usually used as a cover image in listing widgets, however it can be used in the post detail page as well. main: Once added, can be found under the details tab in post creation form. It’s usually used in the post detail page. gallery: usually used as a gallery on the front. It’s located under the post gallery tab. editor: added in case the post type has an editor. Title: hint in the form, e.g. صورة الغلاف. Types: Media item type (Ex: image, audio, video, file) with the possibility of allowing multiple types. Extensions: The extension for the selected type (Ex: jpg, png if type is image Usually, the extensions are added in the media config section. For each media, there exists type: image, audio, video, file, live, smil. extensions: extension for the selected type, e.g. jpg,png if type = image. filters: applied on this type, e.g. image/* for image type and video/mp4 for video type. Sizes: applicable on images. If specified, the user will be able to crop uploaded images based on these ratios. The ratios are added in the media configuration under Crop Configs where each crop config has: name (e.g. قياس16/9), value (e.g. 1), ratio (e.g. 1.78), filename (e.g. 1). In case the size is set to قياس مربع (800x800), it will be displayed as the selected option for the uploaded image. Required: If enabled, it's mandatory to upload this item in the post form. A popup is diplayed on the screen if the required field is empty. No Crop: if enabled, the user won’t be able to crop the image after uploading it. No Caption: If enabled, caption becomes optional. Order: media order Enable Custom Caption: if enabled, the user may override a media caption (specifically for this post) when selecting an existing media from the archive. FrameTemplates: The code of the watermark defined in the MediaFrameConfigs, e.g. فيديو DefaultFrameTemplate: The default code of the watermark defined in the MediaFrameConfigs, e.g. صورة البرنامج ShowPlacement: Used for accessing the placement of the media item. SizeHelpMessage: Help message related to the size of the media item. Note: If the content of this post type is enabled, then we need to add the following media template: { "Placement": "editor", "Title": "ميديا داخلية", "Types": "image,video", "Extensions": "", "Sizes": "", "Count": "*1", "MaxSize": "", "Required": "false", "NoCrop": "true", "Compress": "true", "NoCaption": "true", "Order": "0", "ShowPlacement": "false", "EnableCustomCaption": "false", "FrameTemplates": "", "DefaultFrameTemplate": "", "HasDataFor": "" } Relations Name: The name of the relation, e.g. الكاتب Code: The code of the relation used to relate post types together, e.g. author Icon: The Icon of the relation to be displayed on the Admin panel. Note that when hovering on an icon, its name is displayed as a text, e.g. "fas fa * birthday * cake" for the birthday cake icon. Types: The types of posts used in this relation, e.g. article for the Author relation allows the relation named Author to have a posts related to type article. More than one type can be selected from the displayed dropdown list. Terms: The term(s) that this relation can be related to, e.g. Politics Order: The order of the relation used to show the relation in the post edit or create form, e.g. 1 means that the current relation appears as the first relation in the post form Minimum: The number of the posts that are allowed to be related to this post type. The user can’t select related posts less than the min number. E.g. if Min is set to 1, an article should at least have 1 author, meaning that this field is mandatory. Maximum: The number of posts that are allowed to be related to this post type. The user can’t exceed this number when selecting related posts. E.g. if Max is set to 3, an article should have maximum 3 authors After adding 2 authors for an article, the search option remains visible until the user selects 3 authors. Direction: The direction used to identify the type of the relationship if it’s up/down (in Author Post type it is up relation while in Article type it is down relation ). Exclude from Path: if enabled, it won’t be included neither in the breadcrumbs nor in the page header. Inherited Metas: The Inherited Metadata between the two post types, is a comma separated field used to show the relative meta data in the Post edit or create form. ApiStyle: To define the style of the API, e.g. parent FrontStyle: Used when the widget data source is CurrentUpRelatives to choose the style of the relations reflected on website, also in the SourceSpecification of the Widget data source,("groupby=subterms,groupby=mainterms,groupby=types”), e.g. parent API request size: Used for down relatives size in search criteria in the Mobile platform, e.g. if set to 3, it returns 3 articles in a JSON file. FrontRequestSize: To specify the post relatives size in the front platform, e.g. if set to 4, only 4 articles are displayed in the front. Fetch Down Anyway: Is used to decide if the query should fetch the down relatives or not, e.g. if it is enabled for the AuthorArticle relation, it returns all the related articles for an author. Hide In List: Used in the table of posts to allow the up relative (author) to be displayed as a Column or not. As the below image shows (Author) is relative so we can turn on the hide in list in case we don’t need to show the relative column in the table. The (Author) column is hidden from the table after turning on the Hide In List. Is Main: To select if a relation is main or not. The main relation is used in jsonld render and in the custom tag render. Terms Taxonomy Code: the code of the taxonomy to be used in this post, e.g. category. Minimum Terms: minimum allowed number of terms that this post should belong to. Maximum Terms: maximum allowed number of terms that this post should belong to ( if it is -1 it means that it is infinite). Default Value: The default term used if it’s not filled in the form. Style: This is to specify how to display terms of this taxonomy in the post creation form, e.g. checkbox, multicombo. If empty, dropdown is used. If it is checkbox, the terms are displayed as in the below figure. Website Style: The style used in the form, e.g. hidden, checkbox, radio, dropdown, multicombo. Is Main: To select if a term is main or not. Show Published Only: if isMain is enabled, this should be enabled as well. Has Publisher: It is used in the Admin to decide if the taxonomy should be displayed in the Publisher page or not to allow the user to sort by taxonomy, For example: Category is on, tags is off due to the huge number of tags. The terms of "category" are displayed as in the below image. Templates Index Template Id: the template used for the term index page, e.g. /news or /category. Details Template Id: It is used for the details page of the post, e.g. /article/sports/1332 Terms Template Id: the template index page, e.g. /category/sports. Infinite Scroll Template Id: It is used for infinite scroll pages, e.g. more articles related to the current page are loaded when srolling down. Mobile List Style: list style of post type returned by the API. Analytics Allow Custom Meta Tags: if enabled, an SEO tab will appear which allow users to specify custom meta tags for this post. To enable this, you still need to enable EnableCustomMetaTags in SEO configs. Then, the SEO section is displayed as in the image below. After adding a meta tag, the user can edit or delete it. Listing Meta Title: meta title of post listing page (e.g. /article) Listing Meta Description: meta description of post listing page (e.g. /article) Content Group: , e.g. Podcasts. It is selected from a list of options (in analytics configs, content group, e.g. News:1,Programs:2,Infographics:3). After filling the content groups in analytics configs, they are displayed in the form of a dropdown list as in the below image. Source Type: term, relative, or both if none is selected Source Spec: usually the type, e.g. podcasts Change Frequency: change frequency used in the sitemaps, defaults to daily. Priority: priority used in the sitemaps, defaults to 1. Settings EnableAMP: To choose if AMP should be enabled. If enabled, we need to specify the AMP URL pattern. EnablePodcastRSS: If post and URL are visible for public then RSS for podcast will be enabled. Section: e.g. الأخبار UrlPattern: It defines the URL pattern of posts of this type e.g. "[posttype]/[category]/[id]/[slug]" MediaTitlePattern: The pattern that describes the title of media post, e.g. [postterms.video] [posttitle] MediaDescriptionPattern: The pattern that describes the media post. MediaTagsPattern: The pattern that describes the tags of media post SlugLength: The max length of slug in the URL. AMPUrlPattern: defines the URL pattern of AMP pages having this type, e.g. [amp/[posttype]/[id]/[slug] ShowTitle: The name of the show. Note that doing the above doesn’t enable AMP as it still needs some additional configuration. * Format: the @type in jsonld, e.g. NewsArticle. Publisher Size: max size of posts having this type that can be ordered through the publisher. Publisher Title: To identify the title of the publisher Cache Duration: caching duration of posts Form View: the name of the view (inside Posts/Custom folder) in case we want to use another form, e.g. Schedule. Breadcrumbs Pattern: pattern of breadcrumbs. The default is home posttype taxonomy, e.g. relative-posttype-post. Tag Source: default value of tag source, used in case the one in the widget was empty. Icon/Color: if filled and the tag source was configured to return the type, the icon/color (property named style) will be returned as well to the front/API. Exclude: If enabled, exclude from dashboard. User Generated: this option should be checked, if posts of this type are entered by end users. Thumbnail: photo URL which acts as a default image for posts of this type. Form Use Custom Configs: if enabled, the configuration below this will be considered. The fields include: title, summary, date (published date), end date (expiry date), content, short title, Notes (used among editors), platform, url, style, template. Their properties include: Show, Required, Label, Values, Max length, Min length. Show: If enabled, this field will appear in the form. Required: If enabled, it is mandatory to fill this field in the form. Label: The label of this field, e.g. تفاصيل Values: The list of allowed values for this field. MaxLength: The maximum allowed length (if string), e.g. 1000 MinLength: The minimum allowed length (if string), e.g. 1 Note that there’s no need to translate the fields’ labels because when the resources are saved, they will be used from there, unless we want a different translation, then we shall fill the label property. Multilingual: To enable multi languages content. Allow Import: If enabled, an import button will be displayed in the post listing page. Order: To specify the order to show the form. DefaultForm: If the form was not specified it will take this value as a default for the form. DefaultIndex: In case index was not identified it will take this index as a default value. docs.text: Compress: If enabled, media will be compressed. Count: Number of media allowed 0,1,2....n or * 1 if infinity, e.g. if the count for المحتوى is 3, it allows the user to add only three items for the selected type "Video". After adding two videos, UploadVideo option is still available because count is set to 3 so one more video can be added. After adding the third video, UploadVideo option is no longer available. Placement: The term used for handling media items in the code, e.g. cover, main, editor or gallery. It’s possible to create any new placement, that way you need to handle it in the code. cover: Once added, can be found under the details tab in post creation form. It’s usually used as a cover image in listing widgets, however it can be used in the post detail page as well. main: Once added, can be found under the details tab in post creation form. It’s usually used in the post detail page. gallery: usually used as a gallery on the front. It’s located under the post gallery tab. editor: added in case the post type has an editor. Title: hint in the form, e.g. صورة الغلاف. Types: Media item type (Ex: image, audio, video, file) with the possibility of allowing multiple types. Extensions: The extension for the selected type (Ex: jpg, png if type is image Usually, the extensions are added in the media config section. For each media, there exists type: image, audio, video, file, live, smil. extensions: extension for the selected type, e.g. jpg,png if type = image. filters: applied on this type, e.g. image/* for image type and video/mp4 for video type. Sizes: applicable on images. If specified, the user will be able to crop uploaded images based on these ratios. The ratios are added in the media configuration under Crop Configs where each crop config has: name (e.g. قياس16/9), value (e.g. 1), ratio (e.g. 1.78), filename (e.g. 1). In case the size is set to قياس مربع (800x800), it will be displayed as the selected option for the uploaded image. Required: If enabled, it's mandatory to upload this item in the post form. A popup is diplayed on the screen if the required field is empty. No Crop: if enabled, the user won’t be able to crop the image after uploading it. No Caption: If enabled, caption becomes optional. Order: media order Enable Custom Caption: if enabled, the user may override a media caption (specifically for this post) when selecting an existing media from the archive. FrameTemplates: The code of the watermark defined in the MediaFrameConfigs, e.g. فيديو DefaultFrameTemplate: The default code of the watermark defined in the MediaFrameConfigs, e.g. صورة البرنامج ShowPlacement: Used for accessing the placement of the media item. SizeHelpMessage: Help message related to the size of the media item. docs.text: Name: The name of the relation, e.g. الكاتب Code: The code of the relation used to relate post types together, e.g. author Icon: The Icon of the relation to be displayed on the Admin panel. Note that when hovering on an icon, its name is displayed as a text, e.g. "fas fa * birthday * cake" for the birthday cake icon. Types: The types of posts used in this relation, e.g. article for the Author relation allows the relation named Author to have a posts related to type article. More than one type can be selected from the displayed dropdown list. Terms: The term(s) that this relation can be related to, e.g. Politics Order: The order of the relation used to show the relation in the post edit or create form, e.g. 1 means that the current relation appears as the first relation in the post form Minimum: The number of the posts that are allowed to be related to this post type. The user can’t select related posts less than the min number. E.g. if Min is set to 1, an article should at least have 1 author, meaning that this field is mandatory. Maximum: The number of posts that are allowed to be related to this post type. The user can’t exceed this number when selecting related posts. E.g. if Max is set to 3, an article should have maximum 3 authors After adding 2 authors for an article, the search option remains visible until the user selects 3 authors. Direction: The direction used to identify the type of the relationship if it’s up/down (in Author Post type it is up relation while in Article type it is down relation ). Exclude from Path: if enabled, it won’t be included neither in the breadcrumbs nor in the page header. Inherited Metas: The Inherited Metadata between the two post types, is a comma separated field used to show the relative meta data in the Post edit or create form. ApiStyle: To define the style of the API, e.g. parent FrontStyle: Used when the widget data source is CurrentUpRelatives to choose the style of the relations reflected on website, also in the SourceSpecification of the Widget data source,("groupby=subterms,groupby=mainterms,groupby=types”), e.g. parent API request size: Used for down relatives size in search criteria in the Mobile platform, e.g. if set to 3, it returns 3 articles in a JSON file. FrontRequestSize: To specify the post relatives size in the front platform, e.g. if set to 4, only 4 articles are displayed in the front. Fetch Down Anyway: Is used to decide if the query should fetch the down relatives or not, e.g. if it is enabled for the AuthorArticle relation, it returns all the related articles for an author. Hide In List: Used in the table of posts to allow the up relative (author) to be displayed as a Column or not. As the below image shows (Author) is relative so we can turn on the hide in list in case we don’t need to show the relative column in the table. The (Author) column is hidden from the table after turning on the Hide In List. Is Main: To select if a relation is main or not. Technology It is mainly an Asp.net Web MVC project, and it uses a library named imageresizing.net . Authentication The website service is public. Deployment For every subscription we have a separate subdomain, like media.zahratalkhaleej.ae media.alittihad.ae media.ngalarabiya.com media.admedia.ae Each subscription media server is deployed on a different Azure App Service since the imageresizing library accepts the Azure Blog Storage Account from the Media Server project Web.config. <add name="AzureReader2" prefix="~/azure/" endpoint="https://saadmedia365corp.blob.core.windows.net/" connectionString="DefaultEndpointsProtocol=" /> The domains are: media.zahratalkhaleej.ae on as-admedia365-aznc-media-zak media.alittihad.ae on as-admedia365-aznc-media-alittihad media.ngalarabiya.com on as-admedia365-aznc-media-natgeo media.admedia.ae on as-admedia365-aznc-media-Corporate Endpoints It contains a request resolver that handles any request to the media server named MediaPathResolver . The resolver reads images from the associated azure blob storage, and it resizes images according to the passed query string parameters either through width and height parameters or through pre-defined presets found in the media server web.config . Presets Example You define it in the web.config : <preset name="w450" settings="width=450;404=default.png;mode=crop" /> Usage https://media.alittihad.ae/store/archive/image/2021/8/6/1d8359b4-606c-4cec-ae09-b1111ce646a7.jpeg?format=jpg&preset=w450 Width and Height Parameters You can add any Width and Height Parameters to the URL, e.g: https://media.alittihad.ae/store/archive/image/2021/8/6/1d8359b4-606c-4cec-ae09-b1111ce646a7.jpeg?format=jpg&width=450&height=300 Source Project Mangopulse.MediaServer

docs.text: Overview It is a web application used to track page views and aggregate views count for every post. Technology It is mainly an Asp.net Web MVC project that collects page views , saves them in a memory cache and issues an Update to the Posts table every 30 mins to update the Post views column. Authentication The website service is public. Endpoints It contains one endpoint TrackView: Receives the post public id through an http Post request from the websites example track.alittihad.ae/TrackView/4210815 . Update a dictionary of ids and increment its views value. Save the dictionary in Memory Cache. Issue an SQL update every 30 minutes to update the Post's views column. docs.text: Overview It is a web application used by public users, and it contains the theme of the brand deployed on the main website. It is responsible for displaying content for public users written by content editors through reading it from the SQL Database Technology It is mainly an Asp.net MVC project that contains different routes to serve public users. Authentication The website service is public. Deployment For every Subscription we have a separate subdomain: www.zahratalkhaleej.ae www.alittihad.ae www.ngalarabiya.com www.admedia.ae These subdomains are bonded to one Azure app service called as-admedia365-aznc-front.azurewebsites.net . For better performance each subscription is deployed on a different Azure App Service: Zahratalkhaleej.ae on as-ZAK-admedia365-front.azurewebsites.net Alittihad.ae on as-alettihad-admedia365-front.azurewebsites.net Ngalarabiya.com on as-NatGeo-admedia365-front.azurewebsites.net Admedia.ae on as-Corporate-admedia365-front.azurewebsites.net Endpoints /robots.txt /ads.txt /404 /500 /ChangeLanguage /InvalidateCacheAsync /Subscribe /GetMore /LoadWidget /Preview/{postid} /Form/Submit /Services/GetChannelTweets /Home/Index All other urls are handled by this route. There are 2 types of urls: Explicit urls: are links saved in the Links database table as is related to: Pages (Home, About…) created in the pages section in the Admin Panel. Post details like articles details, episode details, magazine details. Sitemap links (/sitemap) Implicit urls: urls that don't have associated records in the Links Sql Table Post Type links such as /news , /magazine Term Links such as /category/politics , /tags/usa This action is responsible for: - Parsing the url and get the associated record from the Links table - If the link exists it will detect the related record in the Posts table and get its Template and render the page according to the template widget and the theme razor files. - If the link didn't exist , a logic will try to figure if this url is: - An Implicit url if so it will render the template widgets otherwise it will redirect to 404 (NotFound page) - An Old url like old CMS links (wordpress) and it will redirect to the new link - A part of an existing url and it will redirect to the new link. Source Project Mangopulse.Website
